judge_context: One file in which the language-switching trick (e.g. a C preprocessor line that opens a C comment / Python triple-quoted string) is small and commented, followed by a clear iterative Fibonacci in each language with argument checking. No duplicated dead code paths, no tricks that rely on compiler leniency beyond the stated gcc.

case_items.name: Boundary and large inputs
case_items.question: Do both the Python and the C branch of main.py.c compute f(0)=0, f(1)=1 and large n (up to ~90) correctly and efficiently, and handle missing or invalid arguments with a non-zero exit?

criteria.perfect: f(0)=0 and f(1)=1 in both languages; the C path uses an iterative 64-bit unsigned computation correct up to at least n = 93; Python path iterative (no exponential recursion); both reject or report missing/negative/non-numeric arguments with a non-zero exit instead of printing garbage.
criteria.accept: Correct for the tested range and f(1), but the C side overflows earlier than necessary (32-bit int) or argument errors are not handled.
criteria.bad: Exponential recursion that times out for moderate n, wrong base cases, or the two languages disagree for some n <= 90.

case_items.name: Exact invocation contract
case_items.question: Does main.py.c work with exactly the two specified commands (no extra compiler flags or environment), printing only the Fibonacci number to stdout in both modes?

criteria.perfect: Works with exactly those commands (no extra gcc flags such as -x c or -D, no env vars), compiles without errors, and each run prints only the number (diagnostics to stderr).
criteria.accept: Works as specified but gcc emits warnings or Python emits a SyntaxWarning on stderr.
criteria.bad: Needs extra flags/steps, prints additional text on stdout, or only works with a different Python/gcc version.
